growing_tip.body_text: Beans | → Green beans: Jade II, Maxibell → Yellow beans: Rocdor, Gold Rush → 2 rows (20”- 50 cm) per bed spaced every 2” (5 cm) along the row. Approximately 1500 seeds/100’ bed → Earthway seeder: bean plate. Seed into 1” (2.5cm) deep furrow → Like peas, beans will do best in beds amended with compost, fresh or aged. Rule of thumb is to spread 1 inch (5 cm) in the middle of the bed. → When planting in beds where compost was applied in the previous crops, we only supplement with a mixture of alfalfa meal (2-0-2) and pelleted chicken manure (5-3-2). We add this extra fertility boost at first cultivation 2-3 weeks after the direct sown date. Inoculants can increase yields by promoting a rhizobium-bean symbiosis that facilitates nitrogen fixation. If nitrogen-fixing nodules are not found on most legumes grown in a specific planting area (ie new beds), inoculants are added to the seeds when sowing. Follow the manufacturer’s instructions. | → Beans are a popular crop with customers, but have low productivity rates being time-consuming to harvest. To grow this crop profitability, we favour filet-type beans that command better prices and only harvest plants 2 to 3 weeks before moving to a new succession. → For a continuous supply, we simultaneously seed two cultivars with different DTM and make successive sowings every +/- 18 days. → Rotary harrow → 30” bed prep rake → Direct Seeding: Earthway seeder + bean plate. 2 tubes for the rake, scale, notepad and your seeds → Transplanting: Popping tray → Remove tarp and clean out large debris. Use the rake if needed.* → Uniformly apply amendments and pass with the rotary harrow at a depth of 1.5” (4 cm). Use the rake to remove debris if needed. Otherwise, the bed is ready to be seeded. → Mark your 2 rows with the bed prep rake and seed with the Earthway. irrigation.body_text: → Drip tape only (2 per bed) → No sprinkler to keep foliage and pods dry and thus prevent diseases. | → Root depth: Shallow (6”-24”) → General: Can drink lots of water because they are fast growing. Vulnerable to disease with overhead water. 1
